fixes.explanation: I see why you'd lean that way, friend, since you'd expect sons to carry on a priest's work. But the text says Nadab and Abihu died before their father did, “…and they had no sons; so Eleazar and Ithamar served as priests.” That's the heavy part of this list, and I think it's worth a quiet moment. So the priests come down through Eleazar and Ithamar, not through those two.

Lining people up by birthday sounds fair, friend. But no birth years show up in this passage at all. The text says David divided them “…according to the offices of their service.” The jobs decide the groups.

Eight is right. The text says there were “…sixteen heads of families from the descendants of Eleazar and eight from the descendants of Ithamar.” Do the math with me. Sixteen is exactly double eight. I bet somebody in that room double-checked the count.
You got it, baker. The text says, “Thus they were divided by lot…” So the drawing set the order. I think that's about as fair as a drawing gets.
Oldest first sounds sensible, friend. Here's the thing, though. The text says they were divided by lot (1 Chronicles 24:5). It never says age decided anything, so the lot is the answer.

That's the reason the text gives. It says “…there were officers of the sanctuary and officers of God among both Eleazar’s and Ithamar’s descendants.” So both sides had officers, and both went into the same drawing. Eleazar's side had sixteen heads of families to Ithamar's eight, yet the lots still covered them both.

That's right. The text says Shemaiah recorded the names “…in the presence of the king and of the officers…” The king there is David. So the names went down on the page with the king right there watching.

That's right, baker. The text says this was their order for service “…according to the regulations prescribed for them by their forefather Aaron, as the LORD, the God of Israel, had commanded him.” So the rules trace back to Aaron, and the text says the LORD had commanded him. Twenty-four families, one set of regulations. Now THAT is a well-run bakery.

I'd have guessed that too, friend, since the head of a family sounds like the front-of-the-line type. But the text says they cast lots “…the family heads and their younger brothers alike.” That means the heads and the younger brothers all cast lots. The verse doesn't say anyone went ahead of anybody.
